newsitem.title: UK: Thorn says Q1 turnover down 8.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Thorn says Q1 turnover down 8.5 pct.

text.p: British rentals company Thorn Plc said on Monday its first quarter turnover was down by one percent on a constant currency basis and by 8.5 percent at actual rates.

Chairman Sir Colin Southgate told the company's annual meeting that the strengthening of sterling, at current rates, would reduce reported current year profits by some 11 million stg, of which some five million has arisen since the end of its last financial year.
Southgate, who as previously announced is stepping down and will be replaced by deputy chairman Hugh Jenkins, said the current year would be "challenging" for Thorn.
Revenue at the company's Radio Rentals UK television and video operation was down 8.9 percent on a year ago at the end of June.
The company said the volume of terminations had risen by 20 percent versus last year following an increase in UK Insurance Premium Tax.
The revenue value of its U.S. rental base at the end of June was seven percent down on a year ago. But Thorn said net volume growth over the first quarter was ahead of last year.
